description: Bind names to values and update bindings.
Recognize integers, floats, strings, and booleans.
Convert values explicitly with constructors such as int and str.
Use arithmetic operators and evaluate expressions.
Combine comparisons with and, or, and not.
Index, slice, and transform immutable strings.
Understand input values and display formatted output.
Evaluate truth-valued expressions and truthiness.
Choose execution paths with if, elif, and else.
Repeat operations over iterable values.
Repeat while a condition remains true and reason about termination.
Use range start, stop, and step semantics.
Create lists and use zero-based indexing safely.
Select subsequences using start, stop, and step.
Understand tuple immutability and set uniqueness.
Store and retrieve key-value pairs.
Define reusable functions with parameters.
Distinguish return from print and understand local scope.
Construct lists or dictionaries concisely from iterables.
Recognize common runtime errors and handle expected failures.
Use a base case and recursive calls to solve smaller subproblems.
Read text safely with context managers and process file contents.
Define classes, instances, attributes, and methods.
Distinguish in-place mutation from creation of new values.
Reason about multiple names referring to the same mutable object.
Translate a problem into a correct finite procedure.
Classify simple algorithms by growth rate.
